title: France – Financial consultancy services – Accord-Cadre pour du conseil fiscal expatriés et réalisation de bilans retraite
description: L'objet du marché porte sur 2 lots distincts : LOT 1 : La Direction Dirigeants, Talents et Mobilité (DDTM) du Groupe EDF exprime un besoin pour une prestation d'accompagnement fiscal, destinée à ses dirigeants expatriés. Cette prestation doit couvrir l'ensemble du cycle de l'expatriation : Avant le départ : Conseils préparatoires, analyse de l'éligibilité à des régimes spécifiques comme le régime des impatriés. Pendant l'expatriation : Établissement des déclarations de revenus annuelles, assistance en cas de contrôle fiscal, conseils sur les conventions fiscales internationales, gestion des prélèvements à la source. Après le retour : Accompagnement pour la clôture des dossiers fiscaux et les déclarations de retour. Le service attendu inclut des entretiens personnalisés, la réalisation des déclarations fiscales françaises au départ et au retour, des simulations fiscales, la rédaction de courriers administratifs. La prestation s'adresse à environ 40 dirigeants par an, majoritairement issus d'EDF SA, mais pouvant inclure des dirigeants expatriés en provenance d’autres entités du Groupe. L'enjeu est de sécuriser leur situation fiscale, de minimiser les risques et de garantir une transition fluide et sereine pour ces collaborateurs stratégiques. La flexibilité et la réactivité du prestataire sont essentielles pour s'adapter aux spécificités de chaque situation individuelle et aux évolutions législatives. LOT 2 : La Direction Dirigeants, Talents et Mobilité (DDTM) du Groupe EDF recherche un prestataire pour la réalisation de bilans retraite individualisés à destination de ses dirigeants. Ce besoin s'inscrit dans une démarche d'accompagnement et de sécurisation de la fin de carrière de ses collaborateurs clés, en leur fournissant une visibilité claire et des conseils personnalisés sur leur future retraite. Environ 250 dirigeants sont éligibles à cette prestation (estimation d’environ 40 à 50 bilans retraite / an), d'EDF SA et d’ENEDIS. Elle doit inclure plusieurs volets essentiels : Analyse exhaustive des droits : Recensement et vérification des droits acquis dans tous les régimes (base, complémentaire, surcomplémentaire, épargne salariale, etc.), y compris les spécificités du régime des IEG. Projections financières : Calculs détaillés des montants de pensions à différentes dates de départ à la retraite, avec des scénarios personnalisés. Plan d'action individualisé : Conseils sur les meilleures stratégies pour optimiser les droits, rachat de trimestres, impact des dispositifs de fin de carrière (temps partiel senior, etc.). Accompagnement administratif : Aide à la constitution des dossiers de liquidation. Information collective : Organisation de webinaires thématiques pour sensibiliser les dirigeants aux enjeux de la retraite. Le prestataire devra également assurer un reporting régulier et détaillé à EDF, permettant un suivi précis de l'avancement des bilans et des retours des dirigeants.

description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, on behalf of the Durham VA Medical Center intends to enter into a sole source procurement with Phillips Healthcare a division of Philips North America LLC, 414 Union Street, Philips Plaza 6th Floor, Nashville, TN 37219. NAICS code 339112-Surgical and Medical Instrument Manufacturing. The proposed contract action is to provide a service agreement for the Xper IM Flex Cardio R2.x system at the Durham VAMC. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1 using the procedures under RFO FAR 13.106-1 (b), Soliciting from a single source. Contract will be for a period of performance of 01 Dec. 2026 through 30 Nov. 2027. This notice of intent is not a request for quotation. Interested parties may identify their interest in the requirement and capabilities to monique.cordero@va.gov no later than 10:00 AM EST, Oct. 5, 2026. Telephone inquirers will not be accepted. All information shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Gray market items are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) goods sold through unauthorized channels in direct competition with authorized distributors. This procurement is for a service agreement for the Xper IM Flex Cardio R2.x system that covers hardware and software. No remanufacture or gray market items will be acceptable. Vendor shall be an OEM, authorized dealer, authorized distributor or authorized reseller for the proposed medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment (i.e., replacement parts), verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the OEM, such that the OEM s warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty and service associated with the medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions. The delivery of gray market items to the VA in the fulfillment of an order/award constitutes a breach of contract. Accordingly, the VA reserves the right to enforce any of its contractual remedies. This includes termination of contract or, solely at the VA s election, allowing the Vendor to replace, at no cost to the Government, any remanufactured or gray market item(s) delivered to the VA medical facility upon discovery of such items. No solicitation will be made. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to complete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Organist Services at James Lovell FHCC
description: This is not a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, bids, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Great Lakes Acquisition Center (GLAC) is soliciting businesses for Organist Services for Catholic and Protestant Religious Ceremonies (Mass) to the beneficiaries of the Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center located in North Chicago, IL. The contractor shall provide religious music, using either piano or organ, during Protestant/Catholic services on all Sundays and when requested on special holidays. The contractor shall provide this service for Veterans and their families attending Protestant/Catholic worship services. It is understood that all firms submitting a response to this Sources Sought shall be established businesses, and a minimum of 360 hours of music experience in a traditional church setting while performing these types of services. The Contractor shall provide an experienced Organist that can read sheet music, and who can play diverse Protestant and Catholic Hymns during church services. The work schedule hours of service are not to exceed 6 sessions per month. A session is defined as (1) one hour in duration. The specific work schedule will be determined by the Chaplain. Due to the nature of the setting, delays in performance of work may be experienced. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other unforeseen matters. When contract employees report to the facility but are unable to perform services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for one (1) session. Normally, any remaining sessions for that day will be suspended and the contractor will be free to leave and the contractor will not be paid for remaining unperformed sessions. However, if the facility requests that the contractor remain at the facility for eventual performance, the contractor shall be paid for such sessions. However, should such a requirement materialize, no basis for claims against the Government will arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought Notice, nor the Government�s use of such information as either part of our evaluation process, nor in developing specifications for any subsequent requirement. 3.0 Background Walter Reed National Military Medical Center (WRNMMC) Department of Pathology operates a high-volume inpatient and outpatient clinical, anatomical, and pathological laboratory serving military beneficiaries and their families. The laboratory processes thousands of diagnostic tests daily across multiple disciplines including hematology, coagulation, chemistry, immunology, and blood banking. These critical laboratory services directly support patient diagnosis, treatment decisions, and ongoing care for service members, retirees, and their dependents. WRNMMC clinical laboratory requires a secure, reliable middleware solution to integrate multiple laboratory analyzers with the Military Health System Genesis (MHS Genesis) Laboratory Information System (LIS). These analyzers include hematology instruments, coagulation analyzers, chemistry platforms, immunoassay systems, and blood bank equipment located at the WRNMMC Clinical Laboratory in Bethesda, Maryland. The laboratory is required to maintain continuous operations 24 hours per day, 7 days per week to support emergency, inpatient, and outpatient testing needs. Additionally, the laboratory must maintain compliance with Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) regulations, College of American Pathologists (CAP) accreditation standards, and Department of Defense quality management requirements, which mandate ongoing test proficiency, method validation, quality control monitoring, and data integrity verification. Without an effective middleware solution, the laboratory faces significant operational challenges including manual data entry errors that compromise patient safety, workflow inefficiencies that delay critical test results, inability to perform automated result validation and quality control monitoring, and potential regulatory compliance failures. The laboratory processes thousands of diagnostic tests daily across multiple disciplines including hematology, coagulation, chemistry, immunology, and blood banking. These critical laboratory services directly support patient diagnosis, treatment decisions, and ongoing care for service members, retirees, and their dependents. WRNMMC clinical laboratory requires a secure, reliable middleware solution to integrate multiple laboratory analyzers with the Military Health System Genesis (MHS Genesis) Laboratory Information System (LIS). These analyzers include hematology instruments, coagulation analyzers, chemistry platforms, immunoassay systems, and blood bank equipment located at the WRNMMC Clinical Laboratory in Bethesda, Maryland. The laboratory is required to maintain continuous operations 24 hours per day, 7 days per week to support emergency, inpatient, and outpatient testing needs. Additionally, the laboratory must maintain compliance with Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) regulations, College of American Pathologists (CAP) accreditation standards, and Department of Defense quality management requirements, which mandate ongoing test proficiency, method validation, quality control monitoring, and data integrity verification. Without an effective middleware solution, the laboratory faces significant operational challenges including manual data entry errors that compromise patient safety, workflow inefficiencies that delay critical test results, inability to perform automated result validation and quality control monitoring, and potential regulatory compliance failures. Des Weiteren behält sich der Auftraggeber eine optionale Verlängerung der Rahmenvereinbarung bis zum 31.12.2033 vor. title: Sources Sought / Market Intelligence: Multi-Projects for Army Reserve Program � Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and planning purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Project Proposals (RPP), and no formal solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any contract or agreement because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal or bid should a formal solicitation or project announcement be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not governed by FAR-based small business set-aside regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research purposes to assist the Government in understanding the industrial base demographics and capability.) Small Business Size Standard: $45.0 Million PROGRAM & PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, is conducting market intelligence to assess industry interest, capability, and commercial best practices for delivering multiple military construction (MILCON) / sustainment projects for the Army Reserve program utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) executed under Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Louisville District intends to award three separate, standalone OT agreements (one per project), while using this consolidated RFI to survey industry capacity and interest in CM@Risk with OTA across multiple projects within the Army Reserve portfolio. The projects under evaluation include: Project 1: Collective Training Enlisted Barracks � Devens Reserve Forces Training Area (Devens AR), MA Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $35,000,000 � $45,000,000 Scope of Work Summary: Construction of a 300 Soldier open-bay Collective Training (CT) Barracks on Devens Reserve Forces Training Area (DRFTA), Devens, MA. Barracks will consist of open bay sleeping rooms, gang latrines, storage, team rooms, laundry, restrooms, and shower facilities. The project will include information systems, fire protection and suppression, and energy monitoring control system connection. Supporting facilities include site development, utilities and connections, lighting, paving, walks, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, landscaping and signage. Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning will be provided. Measures in accordance with the Department of Defense (DoD) Minimum Antiterrorism for Buildings standards will be provided. Sustainability, energy, and cybersecurity measures will be provided as will furnishings, equipment, and accessibility for the disabled. The facility will be designed for a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-2 including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated building systems. This facility is estimated at 46,000 SF Current Design Status: Awarded separate barracks project at Devens in Sep 2026 with full design. Will go to 65% for this after survey and Geotech. Anticipated CMAR Entry Point: ~65% or ~95% Design Project 2: Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) Facility � Fort Sheridan, IL Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $30,000,000 � $40,000,000 Scope of Work Summary: Construct a 19,000 SF Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) shop at the Philip H. Sheridan Armed Forces Reserve Center (AFRC), Fort Sheridan, IL. The facility will be designed in accordance with the Army Reserve Design Guide, applicable Unified Facility Criteria (UFC) and consists of a high bay drive-thru shop area with supporting admin area. Supporting facilities include organizational parking, concrete aprons, vehicle wash rack/platform, bi-level equipment loading ramp, fencing, walks, signage, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, information systems, and utility connections. Work shall include land clearing, demolition of the existing 26,845 SF AMSA, built in 1939 of CMU, Concrete and steel truss roof construction. Sustainability/Energy and cybersecurity measures are included. All fixtures, furnishings, and equipment will be provided. Antiterrorism force protection and physical security measures will be incorporated into the design including minimum standoff distances from roads, parking areas and vehicle unloading areas. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-02 including energy efficiencies, building envelope, and integrated building systems performance. title: Electrical and Electronic Properties Measuring and Testing Instruments
description: Description Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division is conducting market research to identify capable sources for an integrated radio-frequency (RF) test-equipment capability supporting aircraft electronic-warfare system integration and test. The Government requires a complete solution capable of: Importing, storing, processing, streaming, and playing back the Government�s existing I/Q data files; Recording and Generating RF signals from applicable I/Q data while preserving required data integrity and signal fidelity; Interfacing between the I/Q recorder, RF signal generator, and the Government�s existing signal and spectrum analyzer test architecture; and Providing all required hardware, software licenses, interfaces, cables, installation, integration, and support necessary for an operational configuration. The Government�s existing test architecture includes an R&S FSW67 signal and spectrum analyzer requiring a digital-I/Q streaming-interface upgrade. The anticipated solution must support interoperability between the existing analyzer, the I/Q recorder, and the RF signal-generator configuration. The Government possesses an existing library of R&S-format I/Q data files that must be usable within the required test architecture. Proposed solutions must identify any conversion, translation, preprocessing, or additional hardware/software necessary to use the Government�s existing files. Any proposed data conversion must preserve the required data integrity, metadata, timing, sample rate, bandwidth, phase coherence, and signal fidelity. The Government is seeking information to determine whether sources other than the original equipment manufacturer can provide a complete solution meeting the Government�s minimum requirements. This notice is issued for market-research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Minimum Performance Information Interested sources shall address their ability to meet the following Government requirements: Compatibility with the Government�s applicable R&S-format I/Q data files; I/Q import, storage, processing, streaming, and playback capability; RF signal-generation capability using applicable I/Q data; Compatibility with the Government�s existing R&S FSW67 analyzer configuration and required digital-I/Q streaming interface; Required RF frequency range: 100kHz to 20GHz Required instantaneous bandwidth: 1GHz with 12 bits I/Q and 512MHz with 16 bits I/Q Required I/Q sample rate and data throughput: 1200Msamples/s Required storage capacity: 15 TB Required modulation, pulse, waveform, and output-performance functions: Amplitude, Frequency, Phase, Pulse and I/Q modulations. Maximum RF output power levels greater than or equal to 20dBm across the frequency range. Required RF, Ethernet, digital-I/Q, and other interfaces: 10 Gigabit Ethernet, 40 Gigabit Ethernet and USB 3.0 Delivery, installation, integration, training, calibration, warranty, and sustainment-support requirements; and End-to-end Government acceptance testing using representative Government-furnished I/Q data. Requested Capability Statement Content Interested sources shall submit a capability statement containing: Company name, address, UEI, CAGE code, business size/status, and point of contact; Identification of the source as the OEM, an authorized distributor, authorized reseller, or other provider; A description of the proposed end-to-end technical solution; Identification of all proposed hardware, software, licenses, adapters, interfaces, cables, and ancillary services; Technical evidence demonstrating compatibility with the Government�s existing I/Q data files and test architecture; Identification of any file conversion or preprocessing required and its effect on data integrity and signal fidelity; A description of compatibility with the existing R&S FSW67 configuration and the required digital-I/Q streaming capability; Evidence of prior successful performance of comparable I/Q recording, processing, streaming, playback, and RF signal-generation capabilities; Estimated delivery lead time and a description of installation, integration, training, calibration, warranty, and sustainment support; and A statement whether the source can provide the complete requirement as described in this notice. Response Instructions Capability statements are due no later than 02 October 2026, 8:00AM PDT. Submit responses by e-mail to: Primary Point of Contact: Stephanie Amoni, stephanie.j.amoni.civ@us.navy.mil, 564-230-3333 Secondary Point of Contact: Brian Gillead, larry.b.gillead.civ@us.navy.mil, 760-977-2174 Use the following e-mail subject line: Sources Sought Response � N6893627Q5001� I/Q Test Equipment Capability The Government will review timely responses to assess the availability of capable sources and to inform its acquisition strategy. Responses shall not be returned. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of a response. Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at https://sam.gov/.

This procurement is in support of the MQ-4C Triton Unmanned Air Systems (UAS) Program Unite States Navy. The Universal Lifting Sling is a designated Aviation Critical Safety Item. For companies interested in becoming an approved source, a Source Approval Request (SAR) is necessary, which involved the submission of a SAR package. This RFI does not commit the Government to award a contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government WILL NOT pay for any information received in response to this RFI, and the Government will not compensate the respondent for any cost incurred in developing the response to this RFI. Respondents are notified that a formal solicitation may be announced under a separate SAM announcement. Any requests for copies of solicitations will not be addressed since this is an RFI, not an IFB, RFP or RFQ. Responses will be treated as information only, and not as proposals. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP. Any comments provided may or may not be included in a formal solicitation. The Government will not release any information marked with a proprietary legend received in response to this RFI to any firms, agencies or individuals outside the Government without written permission in accordance with the legend. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. All interested parties should send company information and descriptive literature on currently available products that meet the Navy's requirements, as described above. With the response, include a point of contact, phone number, email address, website information, CAGE code, and Business Size Status for the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code of this RFI. Any responses in reference to this RFI shall be submitted electronically to the Point of Contact associated with this RFI no later than the requested responses date.

title: Airfield Civil Works IDIQ
description: This is the official solicitation for the Tyndall Air Force Base Airfield Civil Works Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) requirement. The points of contact (POCs) for this pre-solicitation are SrA Frances Montgomery at (850)283-8640 or frances.motngomery@us.af.mil, Mr. Joseph Petersen at (850)283-8618 or joseph.petersen.3@us.af.mil, and Mrs. Tanya Gutka at (850)283-8650 or tanya.gutka@us.af.mil. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237310 Highway, Street, and Bridge Construction and the Product Service Code (PSC) Z2BD Repair or Alteration of Airport Runways and Taxiways Services. The small business size standard under NAICS 237310 is $45,000,000.00. The Department of the Air Force anticipates issuing a solicitation for a comprehensive Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to execute various civil works projects on the active airfield at Tyndall AFB where specific requirements and quantities will be established via individual Task Orders throughout the five-year ordering period (base year and four option years). The scope of work encompasses the demolition, repair, and new construction of heavy-load airfield pavements, including Portland Cement Concrete (PCC), Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), and interlocking pavers. Associated civil infrastructure tasks include earthwork, subgrade preparation, and grading. Key Operational and Environmental Constraints: This requirement necessitates operating within a highly restricted, active military flightline environment. The successful contractor must possess the proven capability to: Execute complex construction phasing that minimizes operational downtime for active runways and taxiways; maintain rigorous flightline safety protocols; including comprehensive Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention and dynamic coordination with Air Traffic Control (ATC) and Airfield Management; achieve strict adherence to Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) for heavy aircraft loading and DoD safety manual EM 385-1-1; manage complex environmental compliance; including securing Environmental Resource Permits (ERP) and safely handling, containing, and disposing of contaminated soils and groundwater, specifically in areas impacted by Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF). All potential offerors will submit proposals through the PIEE Solicitation module. Proposals are due NLT 05 OCT 26 at 09:30 AM CDT. Questions are due NLT 08 SEP 26 at 10:00 AM CDT.

title: C-5 SEALS SUCCESSOR PROJECT
description: DLA WEAPONS SUPPORT - RICHMOND is issuing this sources sought as a means of conducting market research to identify potential small business suppliers for C-5 aircraft seals (see attached NSN list) for supporting global DoD customer needs. This exploration may lead to multiple contracts. The Request for Proposal for this small business set-aside is anticipated to be awarded in September 2027. Contracts will be for a period of 5 years. Technical Orders and Qualification Requirements are not available. Potential sources shall be capable of furnishing all labor, materials, facilities and equipment required to accomplish the new manufacture of the item(s). Generally, this entails the procurement/manufacture of component parts, inspection, testing, preservation/packaging, and shipping. The C-5 Galaxy, a large military transport aircraft crucial for the US Air Force's heavy airlift capability, relies on seals for preventing air and pressure flow out of the aircraft allowing it to maintain pressure at altitude and giving the desired aerodynamic qualities to the wing and moving components. This initiative aims to ensure a high supply of quality C-5 seals to support the 90-day production flow schedule. Seals furnished under this effort must be products that are authorized by the qualifying activity for listing on the applicable source qualification list (SQL) before contract award. The C-5 engineers at Warner-Robbins Air Logistics Complex (WR-ALC) developed a source qualification statement (SQS) for this purpose to qualify offerors for the SQL. Offerors must demonstrate their capability to manufacture seals to the engineering source activity (ESA) as described in the SQS. Those offerors deemed technically qualified will be added to the source approval worksheet. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. Unit prices will be established at the time of contract award. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 336413. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with tight program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of key personnel and risk mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by October 5, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to andrew.collins@dla.mil. If you have any questions concerning this opportunity, please contact: andrew.collins@dla.mil.

title: MNNG Mobile Dental Services
description: 1. The Minnesota Army National Guard at Camp Ripley Training Center (CRTC), Little Falls, Minnesota is publicizing this SOURCES SOUGHT notice gathering information with respect to dentistry background and experience. 2. Set-Aside Determination: The Government is utilizing this market research to verify if there is a reasonable expectation of obtaining competitive offers from two or more responsible small business concerns. The results of this market research will be used to finalize the determination for a Total Small Business Set-Aside. 3. No solicitation is being issued currently. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation for Bid (IFB) and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered proposals, nor will any award be made because of this SOURCES SOUGHT. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice. Any future solicitation, including specifications and/or Performance Work Statement will be made available on the Contract Opportunities website (https://sam.gov). Interested parties are solely responsible for monitoring the website for release of a solicitation package and/or any updates and/or amendments. 4. The Government is seeking to identify qualified, experienced, and interested businesses capable of performing the work described below: a. The Contractor shall be able to provide Dentist for medical readiness support services to the Minnesota Army National Guard (MNARNG). In support of this mission the Contractor shall: Abide by Privacy Act and HIPAA regulations and guidelines. Obtain services through a reputable dental provider that can successfully perform these services in a mobile environment and can assess large groups of Soldiers in an efficient fashion. These services will provide dental exams and procedures necessary to meet Department of the Army standards to meet readiness and deployability standards to ensure mission capability of the MNARNG. The contractor shall provide all qualified personnel, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary to perform dentist service support operations. The contractor shall develop and maintain an effective Quality Control Plan (QCP) to ensure services are performed, as well as develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent and ensure non-recurrence of defective services. b. This service is intended to service 8,500 service members during the 1-year duration and have 3 main locations: Cottage Grove, Arden Hills and Camp Ripley Training Center (with the ability to provide mobile support to other designated MNARNG locations if necessary.) The dental service frequency is estimated at 4 days per month at any of the various locations. The Government anticipates a period of performance of a one (1) year Firm Fixed Price contract. 5. This contract is considered mission essential. 6. The following NAICS Code applies to this SOURCES SOUGHT:621210 � Offices of Dentists. The size standard for this NAICS code is $9M. PSC: Q503 - DENTISTRY SERVICES. 7. If your firm has an interest in proposing on the potential future requirement as described above, please prepare and submit a Capability Statement to: Mrs. Ariel Gould at ariel.d.gould.civ@army.mil prior to 10:00 AM Central Daylight Time on 05 October 2026. Your capability statement should be limited to five (5) pages. At a minimum, your capability statement should include skills, experience, knowledge, and licensure to perform the services described. Please include the following: Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, email address, CAGE code and UEID from SAM. Company�s business size and/or socioeconomic status (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Emerging Small Business, SBA Certified 8a Participant, SBA Certified HUBZone, Small Disadvantaged Business, SBA Certified Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, SBA Certified Veteran Owned Small Business, SBA Certified Women-Owned Small Business, SBA Certified Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business). Please note that you must be certified by the SBA to receive a federal award. Self-certification alone is insufficient to receive an award. If your certification is pending, please reach out to your SBA representative to see if they can expedite your request. If your firm is a small business, do you have the capability to perform as the prime contractor? Please address how your team will meet the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). What are the most critical criteria that would distinguish your company�s capability from competitors in a mobile dentistry environment? Does your company currently possess, lease, or have immediate access to mobile dental clinics capable of handling the volume described? Briefly describe your firm's capability to protect CUI and comply with HIPAA protocols in a mobile IT environment.
